title: Week in Orbit
summary: This week, funding continues to flow into the space sector, with notable investments highlighting the increasing interest in satellite technology and resilience. Meanwhile, military applications of space tech are gaining traction, as evidenced by new contracts and collaborations.

themes.title: Funding Floodgates Open
themes.body: Chinese satellite manufacturer Hongqing's $191 million raise and True Anomaly's $190 million Series C reflect a robust appetite for investment in space technologies. This trend indicates a growing recognition of the strategic importance of space capabilities.

themes.title: Resilience in Satellite Communications
themes.body: The Defense budget markup adding $1.4 billion to space resilience underscores the U.S. commitment to fortifying its satellite infrastructure. As geopolitical tensions rise, enhancing communication reliability is becoming a top priority.

themes.title: Military Space Collaborations Grow
themes.body: Anduril and L3Harris teaming up for a tactical SDA constellation bid signals a shift towards integrated military space operations. Such partnerships may redefine how defense contractors approach satellite deployment and operational synergy.

themes.title: Emerging Players in Space Tech
themes.body: Polish company Sybilla Technologies' funding for entry into the U.S. market and Verde Technologies' pivot to space highlight the influx of new entrants into the sector. This diversification could lead to increased competition and innovation in satellite applications.
